_carryNote: Where the weapon rides on the farmhand's body when it is not the thing he just fired: one of `hand`, `back`, `backX`, `shoulder`, `hipR`, `hipL`, or `none` for the weapons that are already on the field in their own right (the Scythe orbits him, the Barn Dog runs about). The anchors themselves -- position, depth and rest angle, per facing and now per CLASS -- are in tuning.json under `carry`; this only says which one a weapon asks for. `carryHeight` is the on-screen size of the art's LONGEST side in world pixels, against a farmhand who is 52px tall: it only ever SHRINKS the art, never enlarges it. `carryAim` is true for the weapons whose art is a side view pointing right and can therefore be swung round to the aim; the 3/4-view tool icons cannot, and are held at their slot's rest angle instead. `carryAngle` is added to that rest angle.

_projectileNote: projectileClip is the weapon's signature round and projectileScale multiplies the renderer's base projectile scale. Every ranged weapon draws a DIFFERENT silhouette on purpose - burst, dart, shell, missile, glob, spear - because colour alone does not survive being 10px wide on grass, which is exactly how six distinct weapons came to look like one bullet.
_meleeNote: Melee weapons draw real art too. `projectileClip` covers the orbiting kind (the scythe's blade); `swingClip` covers the swept kind, drawn stretched to the swing radius instead of the flat tinted wedge that used to stand in for it. The wedge rendered as a large pale rectangle - the 'white square' a player reported as an exposed hitbox, which is exactly what it looked like.

smudgePot._auraNote: The genre staple the roster was missing, asked for by the owner: a damaging ring you carry. cooldown 0 puts it on the SUSTAIN table beside the Scythe, so it is ONE attached projectile repositioned every tick rather than a stream of pulses. `base` is damage PER PASS and `hitInterval` is how often a pass lands, so the card quotes a dps of base/hitInterval; the interval is also what stops a ring grinding one enemy sixty times a second. carry: "none" because it is already on the field in its own right, exactly like the Scythe and the Barn Dog -- assignCarrySlots skips it and the loadout never tries to hang a smoking pot off his belt.

_carrySpriteNote: `carrySprite` is the art the BODY draws, and it is a different question from `sprite`/`tierSprites`, which are what a CARD draws. The six firearms borrow the bundled 132-gun sheet for their cards, and that sheet is drawn to be held by a 32px character: at our 52px a rifle across the back read as a carbine and `gun.pistol.0` -- the Harpoon Gun at T1 -- is three pixels by two. The `carry.*` family is purpose-drawn at 28-31px for exactly this and draws at NATIVE size, which is why every `carryHeight` here now equals its art's own longest side: fit is exactly 1, nothing is resampled, and the number is a statement of intent rather than a shrink. The tier still lives on the card; a carried gun does not change shape when it merges, and six guns that each changed shape four times is 24 more generations for a difference nobody would read at 30px in a fight.
_carryPivotNote: `carryPivot` is where the HAND is along the art's own length -- 0 at the left edge, 1 at the right, 0.5 (the default) at the centre. It exists because a gun that turns about its centre swings its stock through the farmhand's chest as it tracks a target, which is the tell that the sprite is being spun rather than held. Set it at the trigger. It is also the one number the muzzle flash needs: the muzzle is the far end, `(1 - carryPivot)` of the drawn length forward along the aim.
_tierNote: Each tier entry is `{name, delta}`: `name` is the short rider the card headline uses, `delta` is the CONCRETE before -> after the card body prints. The delta is authored, not derived, because half of it is a rider no formula can see (a second blade, a ring, a bleed) -- but the damage half is exactly base x 1.6^(tier-1), which is the merge formula in world.ts, so the two cannot drift without this file being wrong on its face. Before this the card said "Tier 3: +2 pellets (+60% damage)" with the 60% hardcoded in offers.ts, no before and no after, which is the "it is not clear what buying the same weapon three times does" complaint written out.
